title: Change Annals software and contracts
summary: Modify Annals code, CLI, storage, AI-reader, inbox, installation, or public behavior.
use_when: Annals code, tests, terminology, public CLI, storage, reconciliation, inbox, liaison, installation, or release behavior is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use or operation of an installed library.
The change belongs to Nucleus shared execution rather than Annals domain behavior.
Publication or deployment has not been separately authorized.
outcome: A minimal, tested Annals change using canonical vocabulary and preserving exact domain, execution, migration, installation, and documentation boundaries.
effects: Modifies Annals source, tests, fixtures, or documentation.
May require coordinated Nucleus contract work when the requester boundary changes.
Release and installation actions remain separate and may mutate Git, installed binaries, database state, scheduler state, or configuration.
authority: Annals owns works, corpus meaning, reconciliation, history, inbox policy, domain recovery, and its installation.
Nucleus owns shared model execution and authentication but never Annals domain success or retry policy.
success: Canonical terminology matches the registered Semantics repository `annals` and affected behavior contracts are updated.
Affected installation, migration, inbox, and live requester canaries are run when the change crosses those boundaries.
failure_and_recovery: Do not infer compatibility from the shared workspace alone; product release, schema, and Nucleus protocol remain separate axes.
Use guarded installed fresh-state or schema migration procedures rather than ad hoc database edits.
Preserve Annals domain results when later Nucleus runtime failure occurs.
privacy: Tests, experiments, source fixtures, libraries, spools, backups, and Nucleus output may contain retained source and model context.
Do not add contributor instructions or Semantics repository output to the constrained liaison runtime prompt.
steps: Read `semantics.repository.explore`, query `semantics repository show annals`, and identify the Annals-owned contract being changed.
If the change crosses Nucleus execution, authentication, compatibility, persistent state, deployment, or requester integration, run `nucleus manual` before design.
Implement the smallest change and update the owning CLI, architecture, data, installation, telemetry, or Semantics terminology authority in the same change.
Run `./annals/ci.sh` within its product deadline and perform separately authorized live canaries when required.
checkpoints: Current technical and plain-language terms follow the registered Semantics repository while code, tests, and component documentation remain behavior authority.
Annals domain state remains authoritative over model prose and Nucleus terminal state.
Migration, rollback, and historical decoding are explicit when persistent meaning changes.
Release or deployment has not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Select only the contract documents relevant to the changed domain while always reading the complete Semantics repository first.
Use the installed Nucleus manual and current Annals installation guide for cross-system or deployment facts that may evolve.
stop_when: A source or corpus semantic cannot be expressed consistently with the canonical model.
A destructive migration or installed fresh-state cutover lacks explicit authority and recovery material.
An affected shared execution change has not been reconciled with Nucleus's owning contract.
does_not_authorize: Running `annals/release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying or replacing the installed Annals library.
Changing Nucleus shared policy solely from the requester side.
